definitions.gloss: hōhokekyo; the distinctive call of the Japanese bush warbler
definitions.explanation: The onomatopoeic representation of the call of the {鶯|うぐいす} (Japanese bush warbler). This call is strongly associated with spring and is one of the most iconic bird sounds in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鶯|うぐいす}→鶯：29087_uguisu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ホーホケキョ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鳴|な}いた→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。

⟦{山道|やまみち}→山道：12406_yamamichi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いている→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦どこ→どこ：00539_doko⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ホーホケキョ⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえて→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧きた。
examples.english: As I walked along the mountain path, I heard the sound of "hōhokekyo" from somewhere.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧、⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{鶯|うぐいす}→鶯：29087_uguisu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ホーホケキョ⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{季節|きせつ}の{変|か}わり{目|め}→季節の変わり目：22134_kisetsunokawarime⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: On a spring morning, when I hear the bush warbler's "hōhokekyo" from the garden, I feel the change of seasons.

notes:
The iconic call of the ⟦{鶯|うぐいす}→鶯：29087_uguisu⟧ (Japanese bush warbler), transcribed as ホーホケキョ in Japanese. Hearing this call is considered a sign that spring has arrived.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- ⟦{鶯|うぐいす}→鶯：29087_uguisu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鳴|な}き{声|こえ}: the song of the bush warbler
- {初音|はつね}: the first call of the bush warbler in a new year — a traditional seasonal topic
- ⟦{鶯|うぐいす}→鶯：29087_uguisu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{春告鳥|はるつげどり}: the bush warbler is the "spring-herald bird"
